newsitem.title: USA: API says U.S. crude stocks rose in week.
newsitem.headline: API says U.S. crude stocks rose in week.

text.p: U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose 8.44 million barrels in the week ended May 30 to 323.62 million barrels, from a revised 315.18 million barrels the previous week, the American Petroleum Institute said on Tuesday.
The May 23 week crude stocks figure was revised downwards from a previously reported 316.12 million barrels.
API said that crude stocks excluding PADD 5 (Petroleum Administration for Defense District) rose 2.92 million barrels in the week to 256.02 million barrels.
Distillate stocks rose 5.09 million barrels to 107.32 million barrels from a revised 102.23 million barrels the prior week -- previously reported as 101.70 million.
API said PADD 1 distillate stocks rose 1.13 million barrels to 34.72 million barrels.
It said gasoline production rose 261,000 barrels in the week to 8.20 million bpd from 7.93 million in the prior week.
Gasoline stocks rose 2.95 million barrels in the week to 199.72 million barrels, from 196.78 million barrels the previous week.
Percent of stocks capacity rose to 98.4 percent from 96.7 percent the previous week.
API said reformulated gasoline stocks (RFG) rose 413,000 barrels to 38.20 million barrels, from 37.79 million barrels the previous week.
API also said combined PADD 1 through PADD 4 crude runs rose 187,000 barrels per day to 12.49 million barrels per day in the May 30 week.
API said total crude runs to processing units rose to 15.21 million barrels per day from 14.93 million the previous week.
Residual fuel stocks in the latest week fell to 39.85 million barrels from 40.27 million in the previous week.
Crude oil imports rose to 8.37 million barrels per day from 8.34 million, API said.
